subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Universal Motors: AC or DC, It Runs
description: A 60-second lesson on Universal Motors: AC or DC, It Runs.

hook.text: Some motors don't care whether you feed them AC or DC. They spin either way.

buildup.text: A series-wound motor reverses field and armature current together — torque stays positive.

discovery.text: These universal motors reach very high speeds — 20,000 RPM or more, unloaded.

twist.text: High speed makes them loud and short-lived. Brushes wear out fast at those RPMs.

climax.text: Blenders, vacuum cleaners, and power drills use universal motors for high-speed power.

punchline.text: Feed it AC or DC — the series winding doesn't care and just spins.

quiz.question: Why can a universal motor run on both AC and DC?
options: It has two separate sets of windings for each power type
Series winding reverses both field and armature current together, keeping torque positive
A built-in rectifier converts AC to DC automatically
